comparison: Perfect agreement on methodology and sample characteristics (C5, C34-C36, C111-C114). Both evaluations affirm the quality of experimental approaches, tissue source justification, and adequacy of sample sizes. OpenEval notes appropriate citations for epilepsy tissue validity; peer reviewers explicitly praise the 'convincing experimental approaches' and 'solid' techniques.

Perfect agreement on synaptic density measurements (C42-C44, C87, C90). Both evaluations support the stereological methodology and functional interpretation of high density indicating robust connectivity. OpenEval notes caution due to large standard deviations; peer reviewers affirm the 'convincing experimental approaches' and 'solid' analyses without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on astrocytic coverage interpretation (C13, C89). Both evaluations support the functional interpretation regarding glutamate spillover and synaptic crosstalk. OpenEval notes this is appropriately presented as suggestion rather than definitive conclusion; peer reviewer explicitly affirms the conclusions are 'supported' by the data.

Strong agreement on active zone measurements (C53-C59). Both evaluations affirm the quality of structural characterization from 3D reconstructions. OpenEval notes the weak correlation between bouton and PreAZ size requires further investigation; peer reviewers praise 'very good quality' images and 'clear and precise' analyses without concerns.

Strong agreement on astrocytic coverage measurements (C82-C86). Both evaluations support the volumetric analysis and layer-specific differences. OpenEval notes some uncertainty in identifying astrocytic processes without immunolabeling; peer reviewers affirm the 'convincing experimental approaches' and 'solid' analyses without raising this concern.

Strong agreement on background and contextual claims (C1-C3, C14-C26). Both evaluations accept these as well-established facts from prior literature. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and accepted knowledge; peer reviewers implicitly accept the functional context and knowledge gap motivating the study without questioning background claims.

Strong agreement on quantitative structural characterization (C33, C37-C41). Both evaluations support the 3D reconstructions and measurements. OpenEval notes standard deviations not provided for all measurements; peer reviewers affirm 'detailed set of figures' and 'generally well done' work without raising concerns about missing statistics.

Agreement on cellular and structural observations (C28-C32). Both evaluations support the imaging findings and observations of Cajal-Retzius cells. OpenEval notes consistency with cited literature; peer reviewers affirm 'new information' and 'generally well done' work on morphological characterization.

Agreement on bouton size and correlation analyses (C48-C52). Both evaluations support the quantitative measurements from 3D reconstructions. OpenEval notes moderate rather than strong correlations particularly for L1b; peer reviewers emphasize 'abundant and very precious data' and 'solid' techniques without concerns about correlation strength.

Agreement on bouton volume measurements and layer comparisons (C45-C47). Both evaluations support the quantitative findings and statistical comparisons. OpenEval notes p≤0.001 significance for L4 comparison; peer reviewers affirm 'important information' and 'convincing experimental approaches' for structural organization.

Agreement on layer-specific differences in astrocytic coverage (C101-C103). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval appropriately summarizes and contextualizes with literature; peer reviewers affirm the coverage assessment and 'solid' analyses.

Agreement on functional context claims (C104-C110). Both evaluations accept these established concepts from literature. OpenEval notes these are well-cited but specific functional implications remain to be tested; peer reviewers implicitly accept the functional context without questioning these background claims.

Divergent evaluation of RRP estimates from perimeter analysis (C68-C73). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to very large standard deviations and discrepancy with tomography results, noting authors acknowledge this uncertainty. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, affirming 'solid' techniques and analyses without raising concerns about the perimeter method reliability.

Agreement on total vesicle pool measurements (C63-C67). Both evaluations support the quantitative vesicle counting. OpenEval notes statistical significance but large variability and uncertain biological significance; peer reviewers affirm 'solid' techniques and 'very good quality' work without concerns about variability.

Agreement on recycling and resting pool measurements (C74-C78). Both evaluations support the perimeter analysis methodology. OpenEval notes large variability is concerning but methodology is clear; peer reviewers affirm 'solid' analyses and techniques for differentiating vesicle pools.

Agreement on synaptic vesicle size measurements (C60-C62). Both evaluations support the measurements from TEM and tomography. OpenEval notes methodological differences are acknowledged; peer reviewers affirm 'solid' techniques and analyses for vesicle quantification.

Agreement on RRP estimates from TEM tomography (C79-C81). Both evaluations support these measurements as more reliable than perimeter analysis. OpenEval notes lower variability and support for multivesicular release; peer reviewers affirm 'solid' techniques for vesicle pool differentiation.

Agreement on comparative findings across layers (C88). Both evaluations support the layer-specific comparisons. OpenEval notes appropriate comparisons to published data; peer reviewers affirm the comparative approach and provision of data across all examined layers.

Agreement on summary of vesicle pool findings (C95-C98). Both evaluations support the interpretation of quantitative findings. OpenEval notes reasonable but speculative functional implications; peer reviewers affirm 'solid' analyses support the conclusions drawn in discussion.

Agreement on functional implications of structural findings (C92-C94). Both evaluations support these interpretations. OpenEval notes reasonable but speculative presentation; peer reviewers affirm the structural parameters and conclusions are supported by solid techniques.

Agreement on study motivation and knowledge gap (C4, C27). Both evaluations accept the rationale for the study. OpenEval notes reasonable statement given limited prior quantitative studies; peer reviewers affirm 'substantial relevance' given limited anatomical data in human brain.

Agreement on mitochondrial and astrocytic function context (C99, C100). Both evaluations accept these contextual claims. OpenEval notes well-supported by citations; peer reviewers implicitly accept the functional context without questioning these background claims.
